title: Trip Planner
thesis: The first step beyond chat: a model that can save and retrieve trip state through tools.

vibe.name: Cartographic Utility
vibe.metaphor: A route line becomes a state trail: plan, save, retrieve.
vibe.layout: Wide itinerary canvas with a narrow state inspector and map-grid details.
vibe.motion: Advance a route segment only when a tool step completes; reduced motion uses step highlights.

problem: A traveler needs a useful itinerary and expects the system to remember it during the same working session.

architecture.summary: User → Trip Planner Agent → save_trip_detail() / get_trip_details() → Session State

requestTrace: Receive a trip request.
Ask for missing critical details.
Generate an itinerary.
Call save_trip_detail with structured trip fields.
Store the result in session state.
On a later request, call get_trip_details.
Return the stored itinerary or a clear not-found state.
designDecisions: Use one agent because the core task is narrow.
Use tools for state mutation so an action is distinguishable from generated text.
Treat in-memory state as a prototype boundary, not durable memory.
limitations: In-memory session data disappears after restart.
No live weather, maps, flights, hotels or pricing APIs are confirmed.
The trip object does not yet have a strong end-to-end schema.
No confirmation layer exists for actions that could incur cost.
roadmap: Add durable session storage.
Introduce validated trip schemas, timezone and budget rules.
Add weather and map tools behind server-side credentials.
Export a verified itinerary artifact to PDF or calendar.
samplePrompt: Plan a 3-day trip to Hue and remember the itinerary.
sampleArtifact: A structured itinerary plus a visible session-state receipt.

title: Script Team
thesis: A writing workflow becomes an agent team when ownership moves between specialized roles.

vibe.name: Editorial Redline Studio
vibe.metaphor: A manuscript moves from draft to critique to revision through visible handoffs.
vibe.layout: Large manuscript column, slim margin-note rail and vertical role timeline.
vibe.motion: A focus frame transfers between roles; markup appears as restrained redline strokes.

problem: A script brief needs drafting, critical review and revision without one oversized prompt trying to perform every role.

architecture.summary: User → Root Script Team → Drafter → Critic → Reviser; shared output keys and file context

requestTrace: Receive a brief or permitted local file.
Read source content within context limits.
Transfer the task to the Drafter.
Store the draft under a named output key.
Transfer ownership to the Critic.
Produce structured feedback.
Transfer to the Reviser.
Return the revised script and handoff trail.
designDecisions: Use transfer when the next role should own the conversation step.
Use structured feedback so the Reviser receives a contract, not an unbounded paragraph.
Use callbacks for enforceable safety checks rather than instructions alone.
limitations: Routing depends on role descriptions and model decisions.
Mismatched output keys can break downstream handoffs.
Long files may be truncated.
No automatic rubric verifies scene length, character consistency or structure.
roadmap: Add an evaluator with a concrete writing rubric.
Store each draft as a versioned artifact.
Provide a real diff between draft and revision.
Separate source ingestion from the writing workflow.
samplePrompt: Read this brief, draft a short script, critique it and revise it.
sampleArtifact: A final script with a visible draft → critique → revision trail.

title: World Cup Analyst
thesis: Research goes to a search specialist, arithmetic goes to code, and synthesis stays with the root agent.

vibe.name: Match Intelligence Desk
vibe.metaphor: A scouting desk connects evidence cards, calculations and a final report.
vibe.layout: Scoreboard-like header, evidence ledger, calculation notebook and analyst memo.
vibe.motion: Evidence and calculation lanes converge into the report.

problem: A football question may require both external facts and reproducible calculations before a narrative conclusion is safe.

architecture.summary: User → World Cup Analyst → AgentTool(Search Agent) + AgentTool(Stats Agent / code executor) → Report

requestTrace: Receive a comparison or statistics question.
Separate factual lookup from calculation.
Call the Search Agent as a tool.
Handle timeout, empty results and source scope.
Call the Stats Agent and code executor.
Synthesize evidence and calculations.
Present the report with source-scope disclosure.
designDecisions: Keep the root agent in control because specialists are bounded capabilities.
Use code for arithmetic instead of model mental math.
Show source scope because Wikipedia is not authoritative for every claim.
limitations: Wikipedia is not a sufficient primary source for every statistic.
No confirmed multi-source cross-check pipeline.
Code execution requires a constrained sandbox before production.
Documentation and repository dependencies may be out of sync.
roadmap: Add official datasets or governing-body sources.
Attach citations to individual claims.
Use a report schema for question, evidence, calculation and confidence.
Add unit tests for search and calculation tools.
samplePrompt: Compare two World Cup teams using sourced facts and explicit calculations.
sampleArtifact: An evidence-backed report with a separate calculation trail.

title: Love Advisor
thesis: Independent analyses run in parallel, then converge into a structured plan.

vibe.name: Dual-Lens Synthesis
vibe.metaphor: Two independent lenses produce separate profiles, then merge into one structured synthesis.
vibe.layout: Mirrored analysis columns that converge into a centered schema panel.
vibe.motion: Two lanes progress independently and meet at synthesis; reduced motion shows numbered stages.

problem: Two independent perspectives need to be analyzed separately, then combined without losing structure or overstating certainty.

architecture.summary: User → SequentialAgent → ParallelAgent(Appearance Analyst + Personality Analyst) → Synthesis Agent → PartnerPlan JSON

requestTrace: Receive a user description or request.
Run two independent analysis lanes.
Store each lane under a distinct state key.
Pass both outputs to the Synthesis Agent.
Validate the PartnerPlan schema.
Render sections rather than one paragraph.
Display safety and uncertainty notes.
designDecisions: Use parallel execution for independent analyses.
Use sequential composition so synthesis waits for both branches.
Use structured output for predictable rendering.
Treat tone as a product and safety decision.
limitations: The subject is sensitive and can invite overconfident conclusions.
Web search may surface low-quality material.
A forceful persona can harm users.
A valid schema does not guarantee correct content.
roadmap: Add source, confidence and disclaimer fields.
Offer supportive, direct and neutral tone modes only as a labeled future feature.
Add guardrails for harassment, self-harm and abuse contexts.
Prevent inference of sensitive traits from images or insufficient data.
samplePrompt: Analyze two independent preference dimensions and synthesize a structured plan.
sampleArtifact: A structured result with safety and uncertainty framing.

title: Dashboard Insights
thesis: An analysis agent is trustworthy only when claims can be traced, checked, revised and archived.

vibe.name: Operations Evidence Lab
vibe.metaphor: A report moves through an evidence laboratory: ingest, frame, write, audit, revise, archive.
vibe.layout: Dense editorial dashboard with dominant report canvas, QA rail and evidence ledger.
vibe.motion: The report advances through numbered quality gates; revisions visibly return to the canvas.
avoid: upload UI that implies a live backend

problem: Business files need a repeatable path from ingestion to analysis, quality checking and a reusable report artifact.

architecture.summary: Input file → before_model callback → Framework Analyst → Insight Writer → QA/Revision Loop → Formatter; MCP + RAG + logging + archive

requestTrace: Select a file or simulated file preset.
Extract supported content before the model step.
Choose an analysis framework.
Write insights with observation, evidence, hypothesis and action.
Run rubric-based QA.
Revise and re-check for no more than two iterations.
Format the report.
Log tool activity and archive the artifact.
Expose source and limitation notices.
designDecisions: Use a workflow because step order and quality gates must be explicit.
Limit QA to two iterations as a cost and safety boundary.
Use MCP for tool/data access and distinguish it from A2A.
Use RAG for retrieval, not as a substitute for claim verification.
Use code for metrics before interpretation when a real implementation is available.
limitations: A report keyed only by period may overwrite an older artifact.
A shared RAG collection can mix domains or tenants.
Reports may present hypotheses as conclusions.
Hard context truncation can omit data.
The system does not verify every number against its source cell or row.
Documentation and local Chroma paths may be out of sync.
roadmap: Use unique report IDs and versioned artifacts.
Separate RAG collections by tenant, project and domain.
Attach citations to source sheet, cell or row.
Add a claim–evidence evaluator.
Add retention and deletion controls.
Calculate metrics in code before narrative generation.

evidence.label: MCP, RAG, loop and logging configuration

samplePrompt: Find anomalies in this CSV and show how each conclusion was checked.
sampleArtifact: A structured report with QA trace, evidence ledger and archive receipt.

title: A2A Orchestrator
thesis: The final step is not a bigger agent, but independent agent systems that can discover and call one another.

vibe.name: Network Control Plane
vibe.metaphor: A cobalt signal leaves the orchestrator, crosses a service boundary and returns as an artifact.
vibe.layout: Large topology with orchestrator, specialist bank and technical inspector.
vibe.motion: A signal advances through routing, remote service, internal workflow and artifact return.

problem: Independent specialist agent systems need a discoverable contract and a reliable way to route requests across service boundaries.

architecture.summary: User → Orchestrator :8000 → specialist services :8001–:8005 via Agent Cards and RemoteA2aAgent

requestTrace: Start specialist services and expose Agent Cards.
Receive a user message at the orchestrator.
Compare intent with specialist capabilities.
Select a specialist and show the routing reason.
Send a remote A2A message.
Let the specialist run its internal workflow.
Return a message, task state or artifact.
Handle unavailable specialists with a clear fallback.
designDecisions: Use A2A when specialists are independent services.
Treat Agent Cards and descriptions as routing contracts.
Expose service boundaries, timeouts and fallback costs.
Keep the website trace simulated until a verified backend is connected.
limitations: Network calls introduce timeout and availability failures.
Service-to-service authentication is not confirmed.
Agent Card and protocol versions need compatibility checks.
Cross-service tracing is not confirmed.
Hard-coded URLs do not scale to dynamic discovery.
Multi-domain orchestration must not be claimed without tests.
roadmap: Add health checks.
Add timeout, backoff, retry and circuit breaker.
Add service authentication and secret management.
Propagate a trace ID across services.
Use a dynamic registry and capability evaluator.
Provide an offline simulated fallback.
sampleArtifact: A routed request trace ending in a remote specialist artifact.
